title: Introduce heterogeneous momentum load weaver and flakemap exporter
author: Maya Ortega
description: This PR introduces the 'Heterogeneous Momentum Load Weaver' (weaver) and a complementary 'Flakemap' exporter for the benchmark-lab. Motivation: existing runners synthesize steady and bursty traffic well but do not model temporal autocorrelation (momentum) across session cohorts or expose kernel-conditional flaky behaviour in a compact visualization. The weaver generates multi-tenant, multi-model traffic with tunable momentum parameters per cohort, allowing experiments that interpolate between purely IID request streams and long-memory traffic bursts. The Flakemap exporter generates a kernel-aware instability map that correlates intermittent error spikes and elevated tail latencies with the serving kernel and sequence-length buckets, helping debug regressions introduced by kernel selection or quantization profiles. Key changes: 1) benchlab/weaver/weaver.py: new weaver core that composes cohort definitions, momentum kernels, and inter-cohort correlations; supports seedable RNGs for deterministic replay. 2) benchlab/exporters/flakemap.py: exporter that consumes telemetry summaries and emits tiled SVG/JSON flakemaps and a minimal CSV breakdown for downstream analysis. 3) benchlab/configs/weaver_presets.yaml: several curated workload presets (low momentum, bursty momentum, long-tail-primed) used by CI and local profiling. 4) tests/test_weaver_end2end.py: end-to-end harness that validates determinism, basic throughput envelopes and verifies flakemap output invariants. 5) docs/bench/weaver.md: usage recipes, suggested L0/L1 workloads for kernel attribution, and integration notes to the baseline regression pipeline. Design notes and distinguishing behavior: the weaver exposes two momentum primitives: persistent momentum (cohort-level drift where the recent request rate biases the near future) and sticky primer (where priming sequences cause repeated cache-favorable paths). Both primitives are parameterized so teams can stress different warmup and KV cache behaviors. The Flakemap exporter produces a compact view that aligns time-slices, kernel versions, and sequence-length strata to reveal correlated anomalies. Compatibility: the tool integrates with existing benchlab telemetry; outputs are compatible with the benchmark-lab trace-summary v2 schema and can be pushed to the existing reporting S3 bucket or local artifacts folder. Tests and validation: included unit tests for stochastic invariants, a small smoke harness that runs on Github Actions using a reduced synthetic model to validate CI, and a sampling job that generated a 1k-run sample set used in local perf review. Performance impact: minimal on the benchlab harness itself (the weaver is a generator, not a serving path); CI runs were kept light by default and full fidelity presets are gated behind an environment variable. How to use: install benchlab via dev-env, run benchlab-weaver --preset=burst-momentum --duration=10m --out=artifacts/ then use benchlab-flakemap --input=artifacts/summary.json --out=artifacts/flakemap.svg. Rollout plan: land PR in main behind feature flag set to false by default, enable for perf engineers and SRE on-demand, add canary job to nightly to ensure no regression in p95/p99 variance. Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing runners or playback formats unless the flakemap CSV output is explicitly consumed. Related items: ENG-2121 (design + evaluation plan), ENG-2987 (CI integration for nightly coverage).

release_notes: Add Heterogeneous Momentum Load Weaver for generating cohort-aware momentum workloads and Flakemap exporter for kernel-conditional instability visualization. Useful for profiling KV cache priming and diagnosing kernel-related regressions. Defaults disabled in CI; see docs/bench/weaver.md for usage and presets.
